reviews.title: Another scummy company
reviews.text:
I get that every company needs to make money. But Hunch is one of those apps that goes hardcore into monetizing loneliness. 

You get just barely enough functionality to think the app could work for you, then they upsell you all the features that they assure you will get you out on dates. Only to find out 99.999% of the people who “ask you out for drinks” are AI bots, probably created by the company. 

The rates they charge are exorbitant even by dating app standards. $25 a week, with discounts if you spend more for a longer time period. Doesn’t bode well for their confidence in the product if they try to bait you into subscribing for 3+ months, does it?  

I will be deleting my account after posting this review and reporting the ads I see on other platforms as scam ads, because that’s all this and other dating apps have become, a scam to separate you from your money while promising to help you find love.

The concept of 10 possible likes a day is a good idea. You don’t spend hours mindlessly swiping. But then the reality sets in, the app wants to make money. So after you look at 10 matches one day and it meets 0 preferences on anything, and you pass them all, it sends another 10 the next day that don’t meet your preferences. The whole gimmick is to get you to buy swaps and flowers and pay to see who likes you. Like every other dating app, only they hook you in with the “hey we only show 10 people who will really be a good fit based on your criteria” and then you’re lucky if you see 1 who does. Not worth the time or effort to have this app.

reviews.title: Would you like my bank statements too?
reviews.text:
Would you also like my bank statements, 401(k), investment portfolio, credit score, tax returns, and a letter from my accountant?

The onboarding asks for an absurd amount of personal and financial information before you’ve even had a chance to see whether the app is worth using: education, school, employer, job title, annual income, first-date budget, lifestyle habits, politics, religion, availability, and more.

I understand wanting better compatibility, but this feels less like dating and more like applying for financial pre-approval.

Then, after collecting all of that, the app still pushes subscriptions and limits how many people you can actually see. If you’re going to ask me how much I earn and how much I’m willing to spend on a date, at least let me experience the product before trying to monetize me.

The concept could be interesting, but the onboarding and monetization make it feel invasive and transactional instead of personal.

reviews.title: Not impressed
reviews.text:
I have used a number of online dating services over the past 25 years, and I can honestly say that I have never encountered a dating site as disappointing and worthless as yours.
I gave the service a fair opportunity. I was on the site for five or six days and received approximately seven matches per day. Of those matches, only a small number were even remotely compatible with what I had specified in my profile. The quality and suitability of the matches were, quite frankly, shockingly poor. I have never experienced anything like it on a dating platform.
What made the experience even more frustrating was the constant effort to get me to spend additional money. At every turn, there seemed to be another upgrade, feature, or service that required another payment. I had already paid for what I believe was your Pro/Premium membership, yet I continually felt as though I was being asked to spend more.
After less than a week, I deleted the app because I was so dissatisfied with the experience. That’s an extremely short period of time for someone who genuinely wanted to give your service a chance.
Calling the service a disappointment would be an understatement. In my opinion, the entire experience was a farce and certainly not what I expected after paying for a premium dating service.
You can take this as the feedback of one extremely unhappy customer, but I intend to share my experience with others whenever I have the opportunity. People deserve to know what they are actually getting

reviews.title: Promising, but overpriced compared to the current stage of its userbase
reviews.text:
I actually think the app is really cool. This is an innovative direction and I like the focusing and limitation of interaction. The picks in the daily drop seemed reasonable and i have always swiped right on 1 to 3 of the 5. I like that its very date oriented and proactive.

That said, the userbase just isnt there yet, but theyre charging as if it was. $30 for a month subscription or $17 for a week; this is comparable to other more mature products. I have some suspicions that not all the users are real. If a user swipes right on you, you can’t see who they are without subscribing (I had one almost immediately - felt like bait). This feels a bit like a cashgrab.

It also only _sometimes_ shows the distance another user is from you. 

The whole app is built around this notion of commitment to making a date and meeting in person, but there doesnt appear to be any consequences if a user matches and ghosts (which also makes me think there are fakes)

I really do believe this app has potential to rival other apps, but they really need to make the app more functionally useful without a subscription for a while until they can build up the userbase and demand.

If your charm is a large part of your attractiveness, it is totally lost in this app. If you’re not a particularly attractive person, you will get absolutely zero responses, unless they are just desperate. You are judged by your pictures and the response time allowed is only three days before your lost into the void with all the rest. Forget this app. Go find one where who you are makes a difference and you’re allowed to show yourself to others. I’ve only been on a little over a week, and I am only receiving 1 single drop a day, if even that. Some days there are zero drops. And I live in a pretty populated city. Save your money. Go look somewhere else.

reviews.title: Better than getting kicked in the nuts
reviews.text: I say better, but getting kicked in the nuts at least has something to offer. Regardless of what you’re told, expect about 2, maybe 3 persons dropped each day, and your filters do not matter. No restrictions, somehow not one person even remotely available. Strict filter, guess you get dropped someone exactly opposite of the filter. Want them to review your bio and give you feedback? I’ll save you the time…get better pics and don’t be afraid to show your personality. After 3 reviews, I can attest that’s better than the advice you’ll get. Oh, but if you are ok with an escort, don’t worry, you’ll be given their price list before knowing their name. Enjoy

reviews.title: Not the greatest
reviews.text: It’s not a bad app if you give it enough patience. Having the hunch + or an improved package of the app would be beneficial but I’m not that hungry for a date. I will say it’s difficult to even get a match when you ask them out and happen be in line of hundreds of other people who are waiting for an approval. I don’t like that you have to even “wait” around to be liked or matched with, if that’s your style then be my guest but I tried to give this a chance and it’s not for me. I wouldn’t bother buying the packages ethier.

reviews.title: not a free app
reviews.text:
if you don't want to pay for a dating service, app is probably not for you. You can only see 10 people a day, doesn't matter if you're not interested in any of them, that's all you get. What's worse is that even if someone sends you a like, you have to hope and wait they pop in those 10 people per day, as you can't see or match with people who send you a like. Tinder does that because you can swipe on a hundred people a day so there's actually a chance to match; hinge only gives you 8 likes but as long as someone is interested you can make something happen.

This is an app for people who want to spend money on a dating service. Except if they don't make the experience good for a free user base, they'll never get enough people to where the max profile distance can be less than 30 miles... (they also don't tell you how far away people are)

no hate to the app, can appreciate they're trying to do something different, but it's definitely clear they're here to make money first.

reviews.title: Save your time and go elsewhere
reviews.text: As a decent looking guy who paid for “hunch plus” I cannot recommend. Apps like hinge outclass this app 100 to 1. Only 10 “swipes” per day whether you approve or disprove of them. If you disprove? Wait till tomorrow and try again and again and again. It faces the all the same problems other apps do, except it is multiplied since you are extremely limited in who you “swipe”. Paywalls for about half the app. I got a couple matches here and there but nothing special due to the limited amount of “swiping”. Most of the ads you see are fake too so I’d read up quick before you waste your time.

reviews.title: No match
reviews.text: I have not had no matches on here. This is why I think I don’t get any. All the women I find on here are way out of my league. I’m not a handsome guy, not ripped and don’t have a massive amount of money. Just an average blue collar worker. Now this days If you don’t have a six pack, good looks, over 6 foot tall or a large back account. You will have a hard time to find someone. This is why I have more or less given up on dating apps because in most women eyes. I’m not worth their time.

reviews.title: Nothing special
reviews.text: Checked it out for a couple weeks (free version) and there is no reason to keep using it. Gives you a small handful of profiles (sometimes only 1) every day that MIGHT fit your preferences but highly unlikely. If your filters (only 4 of them for free) are too “tight”, it won’t show you anyone for that day and tell you to come back tomorrow. I have 3 hidden likes, just show me those at least of you can’t find anyone new. The other apps give you a chance of having you swipe on someone that liked you. The price is too high for the slim chance it might suggest me someone I could possibly match with. I probably won’t come back

reviews.title: Fake likes to get you to subscribe
reviews.text: So, after downloading the app and setting up my account (at 7am on a Friday morning), I almost instantly received a couple of “likes.”   I could not see who they were and should have been more skeptical (so my fault) but hunch gave me this notification so I could get a month discounted and see who liked me! Awesome! So, I did it.  Only then to accept the “date proposal “ from both likes and send messages with zero response.  For over 4 days. While it shows they are online.  So, you tell me, scam to get me to sign up for that month or legit ?  Worst dating app ever.

reviews.title: Full of fake profiles
reviews.text: First match I got looked off. So I did a google image search, suspicion was correct, the pictures were from an online adult content creator from twitter. Not even the same name as the profile. Did it to a few other profiles and found more fake accounts. And the amount the app wants you to pay money to upgrade is absolutely ridiculous, can’t even scroll for 3 seconds without getting another prompt to upgrade. Don’t download the app it’s just not worth it

reviews.title: Love the concept! Hate the scammers
reviews.text: These new dating apps are cool but they all fail at one thing; accurately verifying profiles. Photo verification is useless as it’s one of the easiest things to trick. Less than 24 hours on the app and I already took a chat to end of life because it was a scammer. The nail in the coffin was giving my Google Voice number and getting the same message from Nigeria and a phone number in Virginia. Guys, stay vigilant out there.

reviews.title: Don’t waste your time or money
reviews.text: I tried this app because I was sick of all the other same old apps, I really hoped this one would be the game changer, nope. I downloaded the app, created an account just fine and liked that it asked a lot of questions about me to figure out my personality, good start. Then about an hour later the whole app crashed, couldn’t log in for about 12 hours. The crashes still happen but seem a little less frequent. I ended up subscribing to the paid service, I set my max range to 100 miles, but noticed all of the pictures of every single profile had unrecognizable city scapes, foreign signs, lots of Asian girls that were actually in Asia. I seem to be matching with every other state/country except my local area. After a couple days of trying it I did not match with ONE local girl and the only actual girl that I did match with was across the US. This app is a scam, they don’t deliver what they promised, the filters don’t filter and I have a strong suspicion that most if not more of the profiles are fake/AI generated to make it seem there are more than there actually are. I tried contacting customer support through their support chat and was completely ignored. Do not waste your time with this app and definitely do not give them one cent of your hard earned money.

reviews.title: Hard Pass
reviews.text:
I just downloaded the app, set it up, set my preferences for distance. Showing me people hundreds of miles away instead of within my local circle. 

Some apps will use this to draw people in and get subscribers until their customer base expands. Seems like that is what they are doing. They have my $20 and I won’t get it back. Seems more like a scam until they prove themselves if they can even compete in the data app space.

Don’t be fooled by the ‘cool new twist on dating’ that they are selling; it’s not true.

reviews.title: Hunch dating- we won’t tell you how far away they are
reviews.text: What dating site has you match with people around the world?  Literally I matched with people 2700 miles away and there was nothing about their profile to tell me that. Then I looked at my profile- doesn’t show my location. And there’s no filter yet. I guess they’re just pre-seeding people to make it seem like there’s activity. They probably don’t have enough users to have a filter at this point for distance. Would’ve been nice to tell me that before I gave the money.

reviews.title: Worst Dating App…
reviews.text:
I have had this for maybe a week at max two… and it is honestly disgusting. I opened the app one day to try it out and the first thing I see is a poll of who looks better, or something like that, this one girl or her sister… One girl was topless, nothing but skin 🤢 and the “sister” was a minor… I was thinking that hunch would have gotten rid of that post because: for one, it’s a dating app. I’m not on here to look at your upper body… and for two: IT IS A MINOR???? 

When I say that she is l a minor, there is no proof of that other then how YOUNG she looked and that she was outside of high school on what looked like the track area. One of the pictures was just her, and not the disgustingness of the… TOPLESS child. And there where a LOT of up votes on the child might I add.

All in all, this dating app is horrible… don’t try it. 
It doesn’t even show you ppl in your area. And I chose to only see men and I saw everyone. Like…

reviews.title: Filled with fake profiles
reviews.text: Even the verified profiles are very clearly fake or AI. I’m assuming these are from the app and not scammers because they’re verified and never want to talk outside of the app. Essentially every match is someone that would NEVER match with you on any other app, and they claim to be from your exact town (which in my case is very small, even on the bigger apps I never see people from it). If you ask for their number or Snapchat or anything, they just try to keep talking over Hunch.

reviews.title: Hate Hunch Now
reviews.text:
I like that Hunch lets you set your age range and distance, but it doesn’t always stick to what you choose, it still shows people outside those settings, which gets annoying. It makes it harder to actually find someone you’d seriously match with.

Another issue is that a lot of important filters are locked behind premium. Thing’s like:
	•	Active today
	•	More than 3 pictures
	•	Dating intentions
	•	Height
	•	Ethnicity

You can’t set any of those unless you pay, which makes it harder to find a real, consistent match. And the swiping limit is frustrating, once you hit the limit, you can’t swipe anymore until the app resets it.

Overall, it has potential, but it feels like too much is paywalled. It’s hard to feel like you’re really finding your soulmate when half the features are locked and the basic filters don’t always work right.
